claim.pdf_says: 14.9.24.4   General rules -- printed at the same typographic level as 14.9.24.1 General, 14.9.24.2 General format and 14.9.24.3 Syntax rules on page 657.
claim.markdown_says: ## 14.9.24.4 General rules   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 28338), while its siblings are '### 14.9.24.1 General' (28260), '### 14.9.24.2 General format' (28265) and '### 14.9.24.3 Syntax rules' (28283).
claim.why_it_matters: The General rules subsection is promoted to the same heading level as its parent '## 14.9.24 MERGE statement', so the document outline shows 14.9.24.4 as a peer of 14.9.24 rather than a child. Any tooling that walks the heading tree (TOC generation, section extraction, the spec-lookup skill) resolves 14.9.24.4 outside the MERGE statement subtree. The same demotion pattern recurs at every '.4 General rules' heading in 14.9 (14.9.23.4 line 28172, 14.9.25.4 line 28544, 14.9.26.4 line 28794), so this is a systemic, sweepable defect rather than a one-off.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on four independent grounds; no content is missing, altered, or reordered. (1) NO TEXT IS MISSING. Rendering PDF page 689 (printed folio 659) at 300 dpi shows the heading ' 14.9.24.4 General rules' at the top of the page, followed by general rules 1) through 4). The transcription reproduces that heading verbatim ('14.9.24.4 General rules', specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 28341) at the correct position -- immediately after the '## Page 689' marker and the running header -- and carries the correct explicit structural anchor '' on line 28340. Every rule on the page is transcribed. The claimed defect is purely the number of '#' characters, i.e. markdown formatting, which is one of the named exclusion classes. (2) THE PDF PREMISE IS MISLEADING. I rendered page 687 (printed folio 657) to inspect the sibling headings myself. The printed glyphs show '14.9.24 MERGE statement', '14.9.24.1 General', '14.9.24.2 General format' and '14.9.24.3 Syntax rules' in IDENTICAL bold face, identical point size and identical left indent -- and page 689 prints '14.9.24.4 General rules' in that same face, size and indent. ISO's house style for these levels is flat: hierarchy is conveyed ONLY by the dotted clause number, never by typography. The parent '14.9.24 MERGE statement' is typographically indistinguishable from its own children. The PDF therefore expresses no heading depth at all, so it cannot be contradicted by any choice of markdown '#' depth. The claim's own wording ('same typographic level as 14.9.24.1/.2/.3') is true but omits that it is also the same level as the parent 14.9.24, which is what the argument depends on. (3) THE CLAIM MISQUOTES THE MARKDOWN. Every cited line number is off by exactly 3. Actual lines: 28341 '## 14.9.24.4 General rules', 28263 '### 14.9.24.1 General', 28268 '### 14.9.24.2 General format', 28286 '### 14.9.24.3 Syntax rules', 28175 '## 14.9.23.4 General rules', 28547 '## 14.9.25.4 General rules', 28797 '## 14.9.26.4 General rules'. The lines the claim actually cites are different content: 28338 and 28794 are the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)', 28260 is '## 14.9.24 MERGE statement', 28265 is body prose, 28283 is a bare ``` fence, 28172 and 28544 are numbered rule text. (4) THE PATTERN IS MISCHARACTERIZED, AND ITS REAL CAUSE IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE. It is NOT 'every .4 General rules heading in 14.9': of the 51 '14.9.NN.4 General rules' headings, 26 are '##' and 25 are '###'. Nor is it confined to '.4 General rules' -- '14.9.NN.3 Syntax rules' splits 14 '##' against 35 '###'. Measuring the whole file, the actual generator is the page boundary: 505 of the 591 headings that are the FIRST numbered heading on a transcribed page are '##' (85%), versus 213 of the 1491 that are not first-on-page (14%); conversely only 8 of 1282 '###' headings are first-on-page. Numbering depth predicts '#' depth nowhere in the document (depth-4 numbers appear as h2 162 times, h3 620 times, h4 24 times). 14.9.24.4 is '##' solely because it happens to start a page. That is per-page-extraction furniture, not a content discrepancy. (5) THE STATED HARM DOES NOT EXIST. The file's '#' levels cannot form a document outline under any reading: 941 lines are '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' (the per-page running header, at H1) and 1233 lines are '## Page NNN' (page markers, at H2). Any tool walking that tree would already resolve every section under a repeated running header, long before MERGE. Structure in this transcription is carried by the 2441 explicit '' anchors, and section-14-9-24-4 is present, correctly named, and correctly placed inside the MERGE subtree. The project's own spec-lookup skill navigates by section number and by 'page-N' anchor and never mentions heading depth. Conclusion: formatting-only, page-break-induced, with misquoted locations and an overstated scope. Not a discrepancy between the PDF and its transcription.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading '14.9.24.4 General rules' is present, correctly numbered and titled, correctly positioned at the top of page 689 (printed folio 659), and correctly anchored as '' on line 28340; the true heading line is 28341, not 28338. The only difference is the markdown '#' count. The ISO PDF prints 14.9.24, 14.9.24.1, .2, .3 and .4 in one identical bold face, size and indent -- hierarchy is expressed only by the dotted number -- so the PDF specifies no heading depth to violate. The '##' arises mechanically because the heading is the first heading on a transcribed page (505 of 591 first-on-page headings are '##' vs 213 of 1491 elsewhere); it affects only 26 of the 51 '14.9.NN.4 General rules' headings, not all of them, and equally affects '.3 Syntax rules' (14 of 49). If the transcription's heading levels are ever to be normalized, it is a global cosmetic cleanup of the page-extraction convention -- which would also have to address the 941 H1 running headers and 1233 H2 page markers -- and not a MERGE-specific or '.4 General rules'-specific spec-fidelity defect.
